                    ### Question

He also has a 1-month history of left shoulder pain. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Physical examination shows decreased breath sounds at the left lung base. An x-ray of the chest shows a 3-cm perihilar mass and elevation of the left hemidiaphragm. This patient's symptoms are most likely caused by injury to a nerve that also innervates which of the following structures?

                    ### Options

Phrenic nerve injury can lead to decreased diaphragmatic movement and elevation of the left hemidiaphragm. The phrenic nerve innervates the diaphragm and mediastinal pleura, so injury can affect the visceral pleura. The patient's symptoms are most likely caused by injury to a nerve that also innervates the Visceral pleura.
